reviewer.name: Oracle
reviewer.role: Independent Oracle applying senior WordPress/PHP and generated-code review criteria
reviewer.wordpressPhpExperience: This Oracle applied the requested WordPress plugin, PHP ABI, generated-code readability, native debugging, and source-correlation review perspective; no human credential is claimed.

independence.statement: Oracle did not implement the reviewed emitter, contribute to the reviewed implementation commit, or prepare this evidence packet.

categories.notes: The reviewed output uses normal namespaces, classes, methods, visibility, scalar and WordPress nominal types, arrays, references, and recognizable PHP control flow without a required Haxe runtime.
The root has an ordinary plugin header and ABSPATH guard, owns activation registration, and registers action, filter, REST, and dynamic-block callbacks through familiar WordPress APIs.
The bootstrap is short and locally inspectable: plugin root, eager local includes and registration, activation registration, idempotent boot, then WordPress-owned callback dispatch.
WordPress-facing methods are public native static callables, helper methods remain private, and the private failure path remains visible in ordinary PHP frames without creating a public runtime ABI.
Hook, REST, render, and private failures preserve native exception class, message, PHP file and line, callable sequence, and unmapped frames; correlation annotates without supplanting native stacks.

The current generated PHP digest is bound by the range map and packet manifest; project-relative source identities and statement anchors locate representative Haxe throws while ambiguous frames remain unmapped.

findings.summary: The supplemental SDK-025 receipt names an older FailureCallbacks.php digest than the reviewed packet.
findings.resolutionNotes: The supplemental receipt records e2612cf416877983e712c930ee6fc0e36ccd3f37c451b964a8f5af990ee7e157, while the reviewed PHP, current map, and packet bind d3534a6374ebec4ded2265850d93fb0be6f2b73c55f4ac213cbb6e811db00dc2. The current map and supplied traces are mutually consistent, so the narrow G1 decision remains accepted; refresh or explicitly label the supplemental record as historical before treating it as current evidence.

findings.summary: The file named autoload.php is an eager include graph that executes adapter registration.
findings.resolutionNotes: The behavior is short, local, and visible, so it does not block debugging. Rename it to includes.php, split registration from loading, or add a generated comment so a PHP maintainer does not assume PSR-style lazy autoloading.

findings.summary: The adapter proof is a bounded Haxe-authored PHP-IR fixture rather than broad ordinary-Haxe lowering evidence.
findings.resolutionNotes: The packet validly proves readability of the exact emitted slice under review. It must not be generalized to arbitrary Haxe source, all WordPress APIs, or production support; future G1 expansion should include a normal typed application-Haxe input and independent source ranges for public methods.

confirmation.attestation: Oracle reviewed all six required categories against the identified content-addressed packet. Acceptance is limited to generated PHP readability and debuggability and does not authorize publication or claim production support.
